title: Poincaré duality and module topological complexity
summary: Topological complexity, introduced by Farber, measures the number of continuous local motion-planning rules on a configuration space. For every simply connected space $X$ of finite rational homotopy type whose rational cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincaré duality algebra, we prove $\mathrm{MTC}(X)=\mathrm{TC}_0(X)=\mathrm{TC}_0^M(X)$, where $\mathrm{TC}_0(X)=\mathrm{TC}(X_{\mathbb Q})$ and $M$ denotes the monoidal invariant.
